key_insight: The paper argues that spatial reasoning performance in agentic VLMs is limited not just by the perception tools themselves, but by the action interface used to invoke them. SpatialClaw rethinks this interface to better support open-ended 3D reasoning.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of enabling vision-language agents to accurately reason about where objects are, how they relate spatially, and how they move in 3D—especially when existing tool-augmented agents are constrained by rigid or inefficient tool-invocation interfaces.
method: Analyzes how action-interface design affects tool-augmented spatial reasoning in VLM agents.
Introduces SpatialClaw, a redesigned action interface for invoking specialist perception modules more effectively.
Evaluates the interface on open-ended spatial reasoning tasks to show how interface choices influence agent capability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that better reasoning systems may require better control and communication interfaces, not just stronger models or tools. It offers a practical direction for improving spatial task performance in multimodal agents.

paper_title: SpatialClaw: Rethinking Action Interface for Agentic Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Seokju Cho, Ryo Hachiuma, Abhishek Badki, Hang Su, Byung-Kwan Lee
